title: Pasta e Ceci (Pasta with Chickpeas)
seoTitle: Pasta e Ceci (Pasta with Chickpeas) | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Creamy chickpea-and-pasta pot with rosemary and lemon
subtitle: Creamy chickpea-and-pasta pot with rosemary and lemon
description: Creamy chickpea-and-pasta pot with rosemary and lemon

steps.title: Bloom garlic and tomato paste
steps.instruction: Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium. Cook garlic until golden at the edges, not brown, about 2 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and rosemary (and pepper flakes if using); cook until paste darkens, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Build the chickpea broth
steps.instruction: Add chickpeas, broth, and reserved chickpea liquid. Simmer 10 minutes, then mash about one-third of the chickpeas against the pot side with a spoon — the soup body should turn creamy while whole chickpeas remain for texture.

steps.title: Cook pasta in the pot
steps.instruction: Stir in pasta and simmer until tender, 10–12 minutes, stirring often. Consistency should be thick and stew-like, coating a spoon — add splashes of broth if pasta absorbs too much liquid before it is done.

steps.title: Finish with olive oil and Parmesan
steps.instruction: Off heat, stir in remaining olive oil and half the Parmesan until glossy. Taste and adjust salt. The dish should read as savory, lemon-ready pasta and chickpeas — not loose soup, not dry pasta.

steps.title: Plate with lemon and parsley
steps.instruction: Serve in shallow bowls with lemon zest, wedges, remaining Parmesan, and parsley passed separately. Suggested sides: simple arugula salad. Hold covered at 165°F up to 30 minutes; loosen with hot broth when reheating.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Pasta e Ceci (Pasta with Chickpeas) with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Pasta e Ceci (Pasta with Chickpeas) on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy chickpea-and-pasta pot with rosemary and lemon. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
